items.title: Permission to seek justice
items.description: Many families of martyrs in the July 2024 coup have been repeatedly rejected by police stations for two years after filing cases simply because the police were named in the chargesheet. Bangladesh Protest Archive has reviewed such complaints. They found at least seven families in Uttara who are still seeking justice for their loved ones.

items.title: Jessore's misery: Thousands of people suffer year after year due to waterlogging
items.description: The waterlogging in the Bhabadah area of ​​Jessore has been disrupting the lives and livelihoods of local people for years. The residents of the area are suffering as houses, roads, agricultural lands, and educational institutions are submerged in water. It is also having a long-term impact on agriculture and daily life. This report highlights the causes and effects of the long-term waterlogging in Bhabadah through the real-life pictures of residents, concerned individuals, and the area.

items.title: Buriganga is taking its last breath, how long will the city dwellers sleep?
items.description: Rafts of garbage are floating in the black water. There is a strong stench. I am talking about the pollution-ridden Buriganga. This river has lost its original form after being used as a dumping ground for Dhaka day after day. Plastic waste is even found 15 feet below the surface. Even though the country's law recognizes it as a living entity, the river has no security.

items.title: Plastic - The waste that has no death
items.description: Plastic pollution is increasing at an increasing rate in the world. Every day, various parts of nature are being damaged. Despite various steps, programs and plans, effective solutions have not yet been implemented to protect the environment. Experts believe that adopting alternatives to the use of contaminated plastic is now the only way to protect the environment.

items.title: About 8.2 million working hours are wasted every day
items.description: One of the reasons for the severe traffic congestion in the capital is the frequent boarding and alighting of passengers without using bus stops. City life is getting slower day by day. According to BUET's research report, every year the financial loss due to traffic congestion is about 50 thousand crore rupees.

items.title: Government building worth Rs 1.5 billion has been lying vacant for 7 years
items.description: On the one hand, buildings built at a cost of crores of taka are falling into disrepair, while on the other hand, the authorities are getting worried after some buildings are built without permission. Construction is stalled for years. In the midst of such irregularities, it seems that the implementation of one project after another is only filling the pockets of a class of unscrupulous groups.
